questions.question: Footrests:

options.text: Can be shared by the driver and passenger
Are required for both the driver and passenger

questions.correctAnswerText: Are required for both the driver and passenger
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Your motorcycle must have passenger footrests. Good footing keeps your passenger from falling and pulling you off too.

questions.question: How can you get sober after drinking alcohol?
questions.explanation: The only way to sober up is time. Your body needs time to remove the alcohol. Nothing else will speed this up.

questions.question: Before riding, check your throttle. It should:

options.text: Stay in place when you release it
Stay loose when you release it
Snap back when you release it

questions.correctAnswerText: Snap back when you release it
questions.explanation: Check your clutch and throttle before riding. The throttle should snap back when released. The clutch should feel tight and smooth.

questions.question: The best way to stop quickly is to:

options.text: Use both brakes at the same time

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both the front and rear brakes with steady pressure at the same time.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the right lane ends ahead.

questions.question: Riding is difficult right after it starts raining because:

options.text: Other drivers may not react quickly to the rain
Other drivers do not drive fast enough in wet weather

questions.explanation: The pavement is very slippery when rain first starts. Oil from vehicles has not yet washed away, mixing with water to create a slippery surface.

questions.question: What should you do if you must ride on a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, reduce your speed, avoid sudden moves, and use both brakes.

questions.question: Your lane position on a motorcycle:

options.text: Does not affect whether other drivers can see you
Is important because it affects whether other drivers can see you
Cannot protect you from wind from other vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: Is important because it affects whether other drivers can see you
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see and be seen. It also helps you avoid wind blasts from other vehicles.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the roadside with flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop on the road behind the emergency vehicle
Stop and wait until the emergency vehicle starts moving
Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle
questions.explanation: If you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes to give it extra space and slow down. Be ready to stop when you pass an emergency scene.

questions.question: When riding at night:

options.text: Ride in the left part of the lane to see around vehicles ahead
Ride close to the vehicle in front to use their headlights
Reduce your speed to help avoid hazards

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed to help avoid hazards
questions.explanation: Ride slower at night than during the day. This gives you more time to avoid hazards. Also increase your following distance and be flexible with your lane position.

questions.question: Can one alcoholic drink before riding affect you?

options.text: No, it will not lead to a DUI conviction.
No, it will never affect your riding skills.
Yes, it can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it can affect your ability to operate a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: You can be impaired after just one drink. You can be convicted of riding impaired even if your blood alcohol level is below the legal limit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns of a railroad crossing ahead.

questions.question: How do you get the most protection from your helmet?
questions.explanation: A helmet gives you the most protection when it meets DOT and state standards, fits snugly all the way around, and has no damage.

questions.question: What is a good way to handle tailgaters?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may increase danger by making them tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves on rain grooves or bridge gratings, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get across faster.
Zigzag on purpose to get other drivers' attention.
Keep a steady speed and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves on grooves or gratings, keep a steady speed and go straight across. Trying to fix the weave by riding at an angle makes you zigzag, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, any sudden change in speed or direction can cause a skid. Accelerate, shift gears, turn, and brake as smoothly as possible.

questions.question: Do motorcycle mirrors have blind spots?

options.text: Yes, they have blind spots, just like cars.
No, because motorcycles are usually smaller than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they have blind spots, just like cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like cars. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What should you do when a tailgater is following you?

options.text: Don't change how you are riding.

questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass you. Speeding up may result in them tailgating you at a higher speed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers about traffic laws in that area. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When should you inspect your motorcycle for safety?
questions.explanation: Always inspect your motorcycle before you ride. A small problem on a motorcycle is more dangerous than a small problem on a car.

questions.question: When riding in a group, how should mirrors be used?

options.text: All riders should check them often.
Only the lead rider should check them.
They should not be checked often because they distract you.

questions.correctAnswerText: All riders should check them often.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often when riding in a group. This lets you see the riders behind you and makes sure the group stays together.

questions.question: What gear should your motorcycle be in when you start the engine?
questions.explanation: Put your motorcycle in neutral before starting the engine. Most motorcycles have a neutral light on the dashboard that turns on when the engine is ready and the bike is in neutral.

questions.question: What should NOT be included in a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, controls, lights, signals, mirrors, brakes, oil, fluids, frame, and stands. Paint inspection is not necessary.

questions.question: When slowing down or stopping a motorcycle, what should you do with the gears?
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears using the clutch as you slow down or stop. Stay in first gear when stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: If there are hazards on your right side, which side of your lane should you ride on?
questions.explanation: Position yourself in your lane to have the most space. If hazards are on your left, ride on the right side of your lane. If hazards are on your right, ride on the left side of your lane.
